appearances.activity: Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's office participated in the Japan-Marshall Islands summit meeting, with MOFA releasing a formal readout; she also hosted the Marshall Islands president at a broader engagement, per Jiji and MOFA sources.

Prime Minister Takaichi on Tuesday ordered officials to draft a second FY2026 supplementary budget for disaster response and met with ICC President Tomoko Akane, pledging to advance Japan's 2027 ICC financial contribution ahead of schedule.

Prime Minister Takaichi met ICC President Tomoko Akane in Tokyo on Tuesday, pledging to advance Japan's 2027 ICC financial contribution ahead of schedule in direct tension with US sanctions against the court.

Prime Minister Takaichi's post-APEC diplomatic activity continues to generate coverage, with the Japan Times reporting on the domestic political implications of Beijing's snub; Takaichi is due to meet ICC President Akane on Tuesday.

Prime Minister Takaichi held bilateral summits with Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori and Chilean President Jose Antonio Kast on the margins of APEC in Shenzhen, agreeing on critical mineral supply chain cooperation, and previously held her first meeting with Russian President Putin at the same venue.

Prime Minister Takaichi concluded APEC in Shenzhen with a post-summit press conference reaffirming Japan's Taiwan position and pledging 'good faith' Diet participation, while departing China without a formal Xi bilateral.

Prime Minister Takaichi arrived in Shenzhen for APEC after holding a bilateral with President Trump in Manila, paying tribute at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier in Fort Bonifacio, and completing the Quad Leaders' Summit — all on November 18.

Prime Minister Takaichi chaired the ASEAN-Japan summit, the 13th Mekong-Japan Summit, the 4th AZEC Leaders' Meeting, and held a bilateral with Philippine President Marcos in Manila, while also completing the first brief encounter with a Chinese official since the diplomatic rift.

Prime Minister Takaichi departed Monday for a four-day trip to Manila and Shenzhen, spoke to the press ahead of departure regarding her ASEAN/APEC agenda, met Philippine President Marcos, and published a contributed article in regional newspapers outlining Japan's Indo-Pacific vision.
PM Takaichi publicly reiterated her determination to bring abductee Megumi Yokota home from North Korea on the 49th anniversary of the kidnapping, per the Japan Times.

PM Takaichi hosted a roundtable at the Kantei with companies involved in physical AI and separately confirmed the government will consider a worker benefit program covering over 50 percent of Japan's workforce linked to the food tax cut bill.
PM Takaichi issued formal avian influenza emergency instructions to relevant ministries at 13:40 on November 11; the Kantei published the instruction on the same date.
PM Takaichi issued formal avian influenza emergency instructions to relevant ministries at 13:40 on November 11, per the Kantei.

PM Takaichi participated in a France-hosted online G7 AI security meeting, calling for international coordination on AI safety, and the Kantei published the Japan-Vietnam summit summary from yesterday's meeting with President To Lam.
PM Takaichi is due to hold a summit with Vietnamese President To Lam in Tokyo today covering energy security, economic security, AI, and quantum technology cooperation.
PM Takaichi attended a Tokyo rally of families of North Korean abductees, where participants adopted a resolution demanding the immediate collective return of abductees.
Prime Minister Takaichi's emergency cybersecurity package was publicly released and she stated Japan is 'vigilant to market moves' and focused on boosting the economy amid the Nikkei selloff.

PM Takaichi conducted a telephone summit with French President Macron to convey concerns over the EU Industrial Accelerator Act and issued a public statement pledging to cooperate with President Trump to strengthen the Japan-US alliance following the US midterm results.

Prime Minister Takaichi issued formal instructions to relevant ministries at 12:38 in response to North Korea's suspected ballistic missile launches, and received a courtesy call from the mayors of Hiroshima and Nagasaki.

PM Takaichi concluded the Japan-Germany Summit Working Dinner with Chancellor Merz and the Japan-Bangladesh Summit, with outcomes released by the Kantei on October 28-29 covering critical mineral supply chains, AI cooperation, GCAP, and a one-trillion-yen Bangladesh investment framework.
Prime Minister Takaichi held a press conference on the passing of former PM Fukuda and confirmed the Japan-Bangladesh Summit outcome including a 1 trillion yen investment plan.

PM Takaichi convened a press conference on the passing of former PM Fukuda, directed the government to compile an emergency cybersecurity package by next week, and her active cyber defense posture statement was reported by Asahi and Kyodo.

PM Takaichi convened a national cybersecurity meeting amid surging attacks on Japanese companies and declared she will 'execute all response options including active cyber defense,' per Bloomberg and Asahi.
PM Takaichi directed METI Minister Akazawa to review gasoline subsidies and is confirmed active via Japan Today and Japan Times reporting on Oct. 24.
PM Takaichi instructed METI Minister Akazawa to review and scale back gasoline subsidies from December, adding a fiscal policy directive to her cybersecurity-related public communications this week.

Prime Minister Takaichi pressed the BOJ to buy more bonds via public statement, met Yokohama's mayor to coordinate on the 2027 horticultural expo, and issued an urgent social-media advisory on PHP cybersecurity vulnerabilities.

PM Takaichi marks one year in office; Chief Cabinet Secretary Kihara stated at the morning press conference that the government has steadily delivered on its pledges, while Diet debate on the food consumption tax cut continued.
Takaichi said in Diet debate that the food consumption tax cut will not use deficit bonds and will not be extended beyond its planned period for economic reasons.

PM Takaichi sent a monetary offering to Yasukuni Shrine for the autumn grand festival and participated in Lower House Budget Committee deliberations, including a verbal exchange with JCP lawmakers over the LDP slush-fund issue.

PM Takaichi is expected to continue Diet deliberations on the consumption tax cut bill; today's PM APPEARANCE reports confirm she sent a masakaki offering to Yasukuni Shrine on Oct 17 and her Diet schedule continues Sunday.

PM Takaichi sent a ritual masakaki offering to Yasukuni Shrine for the autumn grand festival, skipping a personal visit, and is expected to continue the Diet's deliberations on the consumption tax cut bill.

PM Takaichi held two press conferences — one on the resignation of Agriculture Minister Yana and one on ministerial appointments — and publicly denied Japan has conducted espionage activities in Russia.

PM Takaichi held a formal press conference on Agriculture Minister Yana's resignation, announced Arata Takebe as successor, and denied Japanese espionage in Russia in connection with the Hokkaido Shimbun journalist detention.

Prime Minister Takaichi confirmed Japan-US talks on tightening off-duty troop conduct rules, stated she would not hesitate to dismiss Yana if illegality was confirmed, and was reported publicly on Diet schedule and personal schedule remarks.

PM Takaichi publicly raised the possibility of dismissing Agriculture Minister Yana if illegality is confirmed, reaffirmed Japan's support for the ICC and its Japanese president in response to US sanctions, and pledged to finalize the foreign resident basic policy by March 2027.

Prime Minister **Sanae Takaichi** has been publicly active on the ICC sanctions dispute (declaring them 'incompatible with Japan's position'), with Foreign Minister Motegi conducting a follow-up call with Rubio today at her direction; Takaichi also pushed at the UN for deletion of WWII 'enemy state' clauses from the UN Charter.

Prime Minister Takaichi publicly declared US ICC sanctions 'incompatible with Japan's position,' joined a multilateral MOFA joint statement, and the Cabinet submitted the food consumption tax cut bill to the Diet.
Takaichi's cabinet approved and submitted the food consumption-tax cut bill to the Diet, and she pledged to keep watching yen and inflation moves carefully.

Prime Minister Takaichi issued a public congratulatory statement on the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for Professor Emeritus Kenso Soai, placed a congratulatory telephone call to Soai, and in Diet proceedings again refused opposition demands to dismiss Agriculture Minister Yana.

PM Takaichi met Okinawa Governor Koja at the Kantei, pledged preventive steps with the United States over the Marine murder case, and separately defended her consumption tax cut plan in the extraordinary Diet session.

Prime Minister Takaichi addressed the extraordinary Diet session, condemned the Okinawa Marine murder as 'heinous,' pledged a breakthrough on North Korean abductions, and met with relatives of abductees who briefed her on their US visit.

Prime Minister Takaichi delivered her policy address to the extraordinary Diet session, pledging proactive fiscal policy and a consumption tax cut without new bond issuance, and separately told markets to 'rest assured' on debt control.

PM Takaichi issued a formal protest to Washington over the Okinawa Marine murder arrest, publicly describing the crime as 'exceptionally brutal and vicious' and demanding US military authorities take action.

PM Takaichi met with Qatari PM Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al-Thani in Tokyo, agreeing on close coordination for Middle East de-escalation, and separately made a public statement warning retailers against absorbing food tax cuts without passing savings to consumers.

PM Takaichi's draft policy address for the October 5 extra Diet session was reported today, reaffirming the five-year growth investment plan and pledging a nimble FX response — constituting a substantive public policy statement.

PM Takaichi's draft policy address for the October 5 extra Diet session — pledging a 'nimble response to unexpected market moves' and active fiscal stance — was reported by Nikkei and Reuters, constituting a substantive public policy statement.
PM Takaichi convened the first closed-door session of her 17-member intelligence panel and made a public statement on strengthening Japan's intelligence capabilities.

PM Takaichi held a press briefing on her post-Trump-Xi summit telephone call with President Trump, announcing Japan-US agreement to collaborate on China-related issues and describing herself as having received a 'detailed' briefing from Trump on his Xi summit.

Prime Minister Takaichi's bilateral with President Trump and her UNGA engagements from September 24 continued to generate coverage on September 25, with Finance Minister Katayama disclosing the yen exchange in those talks; no new confirmed Takaichi public appearance on September 25 itself is reported in today's articles.

Prime Minister Takaichi delivered Japan's UNGA address calling for removal of 'enemy state' clauses, held a bilateral with Trump, met Turkish President Erdogan to confirm defense equipment cooperation, and separately avoided being drawn into discussion of US ICC sanctions during her Trump meeting.

Prime Minister Takaichi delivered Japan's first UNGA address of her term on September 22, met President Trump bilaterally, and held her first meeting with Ukrainian President Zelenskyy on the UNGA sidelines in New York.

Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi arrived in New York and held a bilateral meeting with President Trump on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, with her investment-in-the-US message as the central talking point.
Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi departed Japan for New York to attend the UN General Assembly, with a confirmed bilateral with President Trump on Tuesday, September 22.

PM Takaichi is en route to or present in New York for the UN General Assembly, with a confirmed Trump bilateral set for Tuesday and a Ukrainian bilateral meeting request pending, following her instruction to the new cabinet to focus on market stability and the Middle East.
PM Takaichi's travel to New York for the UN General Assembly was confirmed, with a Trump bilateral set for Tuesday September 22 ahead of Xi Jinping's Washington state visit.
PM Takaichi held a post-reshuffle press conference recommitting to key policies including a strong-economy agenda, following the completion of her first cabinet reshuffle on September 17.
Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi presided over her first cabinet reshuffle, retaining core ministers and incorporating a Japan Innovation Party member for the first time.
PM Takaichi presided over the LDP executive reshuffle on September 16, appointing a new party leadership team that retains most senior figures ahead of the fall Diet session.
Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi met IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol in Tokyo and called for closer Japan-IEA cooperation on energy security.

PM Takaichi demanded Russia remove the war-victory statue in Khabarovsk and government confirmed the September 16 cabinet reshuffle plan, with Chief Cabinet Secretary Kihara holding the afternoon press conference to announce Japan's response to China's dichlorosilane anti-dumping measures.

PM Takaichi's government confirmed the September 16 cabinet reshuffle plan and the Chief Cabinet Secretary announced Japan's protest and impact-assessment response to China's dichlorosilane anti-dumping measures.

PM Takaichi's government confirmed the September 16 cabinet reshuffle plan, and Chief Cabinet Secretary Kihara held the September 8 afternoon press conference announcing Japan's protest and impact-assessment response to China's dichlorosilane anti-dumping measures.

PM Takaichi's government confirmed the September 16 cabinet reshuffle plan and Chief Cabinet Secretary Minoru Kihara held the September 8 afternoon press conference announcing Japan's protest and impact-assessment response to China's dichlorosilane anti-dumping measures.

PM Takaichi stepped up cabinet reshuffle planning with an explicit focus on US-savvy ministers and lauded the transparency of Japan's record FY2027 budget requests, per Nikkei Asia and Japan Times reporting on her public statements.

PM Takaichi confirmed to address the UN General Assembly on September 22; separately reported rejecting criticism over the revised Imperial House Law and lauding transparency of record FY2027 budget requests.

PM Takaichi praised the transparency of Japan's record FY2027 budget requests and the government confirmed it is considering forgoing a second FY2026 supplementary budget, per Japan Times and Jiji Press.
PM Takaichi presided over the Self-Defense Forces Senior Commanders' Conference in Tokyo and pledged to accelerate AI and unmanned defense asset introduction into SDF operations.
PM Takaichi held a telephone summit with Nepal's prime minister seeking cooperation in the search for five Japanese nationals missing in Nepalese floods, per the Prime Minister's Office.

PM Takaichi held a telephone summit with Nepal's prime minister seeking cooperation in the search for five missing Japanese nationals, and the Prime Minister's Office confirmed FY2026 comprehensive disaster management drills were conducted.
PM Takaichi participated in Japan's annual Disaster Prevention Day simulated earthquake drill, which this year modeled an 8.3-magnitude offshore Tokachi quake, per the Japan Times.
